title: Adericel Issuer Public Key v1
description: A published issuer public key. Safe to distribute; contains no private material. A verifier holding this key can establish the authenticity of any passport interchange envelope naming its keyId.

keyId.description: Immutable. Rotation issues a new id and never reuses one, because a reused id would make a historical signature unverifiable in a way indistinguishable from tampering.

status.description: RETIRED keys remain trusted for verification and are never destroyed: destroying one would make every passport it signed unverifiable, which looks exactly like forgery. REVOKED means signatures made by it are no longer to be relied upon, which is a different fact and calls for a different response.

registeredAt.description: When an operator established this key, as they recorded it. Null when it is not known — a key derived from a configured signing key that was never added to the published keyring. Null rather than a made-up date: a provenance record that invents its own timestamp is worse than one that admits it has none.
